name: Temah
overview: Temah was a male member of the tribe of Levi who served as a temple servant, according to Ezra 2:53. His role as a temple servant highlights his participation in the religious life and duties associated with the Levitical tribe. There are no additional personal notes recorded about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Temah is recorded plainly in Ezra 2:53 without any given meaning or divine attribution. It serves as a proper name identifying this individual within the Levitical community.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Temah as a descendant of Levi, linking him to the priestly tribe responsible for temple service. Beyond this tribal connection, no further family relationships are documented.
scriptureSignificance: Temah's significance lies in his role as a temple servant among the Levites, underscoring the continuity of Levitical duties during the post-exilic period. His mention in Ezra 2:53 situates him within the returned community committed to restoring proper worship and temple service in Jerusalem. Though briefly noted, Temah represents the faithful remnant dedicated to God's house and covenant.
